source: CAMFAD student thesis: "Establishment of a New Coconut Plantation Farm", National School of Agriculture, July 1994
text:
The thesis describes two nursery methods used to raise coconut seedlings before field planting, both started well ahead of the planned field-planting date since coconut nursery seedlings need to reach a certain age/size before transplanting.

Trench nursery method (ថ្នាលដំបូង): preparation should begin about 18 months before the seedlings are due to be planted out in the field. A trench-style nursery bed is dug (dimensions given in the source as roughly 108 x 28.5 cm per row unit, though this scanned figure should be treated as approximate), lined at the bottom with fertile soil, with drainage considered so rainwater does not pool and waterlog the germinating nuts; if drainage is inadequate the bed should be raised or channeled. Seed nuts are placed close together in rows with a small gap between them, and the bed is watered twice a day (skipped when it has rained). Trenches/beds are laid out with roughly 2-meter-wide access paths between them for tending and watering.

Bag (potted) nursery method (ថ្នាលសំខាន់): used as an alternative, more mobile nursery approach. After the nut has germinated in the ground for about 3-4 months and produced its first visible leaf, it is transferred into a planting bag (roughly 65 x 60 cm) filled with fertile topsoil mixed with compost, firmed in place. Bags are spaced about 90 cm apart to allow good drainage and airflow between seedlings. A small amount of Mg (magnesium) fertilizer, roughly 1-2 spoonfuls per bag, is worked into the bag's soil, and wood ash is also used, valued for helping control soil-borne pests/pathogens around the root zone.
